question: closed_to_civilians
answer: unknown; no source found for a declared military or closed border zone covering the exclaves. Evidence points the other way for Barkhudarli-Sofulu: Armenia's main Ijevan-Berd highway runs through it (an ordinary Armenian road).

question: changed_by_2024_delimitation
answer: no. The April-May 2024 delimitation covered only the border section of four non-exclave villages (Baganis Ayrum, Ashagi Askipara, Kheyrimli, Gizilhajili); enclaves and exclaves were deferred to later stages. No later act transferring them was found up to the commissions' 13th meeting (29 Apr 2026).
publisher: Caucasus Watch (19 Apr 2024), reporting the commissions' statement
quote: the delimitation process will be extended to all remaining sections of the border, including enclaves and exclaves
notes: Secondary report of the joint statement; the Armenian primary text (armenpress 1135197) returned HTTP 403. Armenian MFA press release of 29 Apr 2026 (https://www.mfa.am/en/press-releases/2026/04/29/Arm-Az/13912) reports agreed draft delimitation instructions and a signed protocol and does not mention enclaves (summary). So the status as of 2026 appears unchanged; a later 2026 event not found is possible.

question: closed_to_civilians
answer: effectively closed on the Israeli-held side, but no named closure order found: Israeli roads to Mount Dov (Har Dov, Israel's name for the northern part of Shebaa Farms) are not open to regular civilian traffic; civilians reached the lookout only on IDF-escorted organised tours on authorised dates (Sukkot, autumn 2026).
publisher: Ynet (Yedioth Ahronoth), undated, photos dated 29-30 Sep 2026
quote: summary: "The roads leading to Mount Dov have not yet been opened to regular civilian traffic"; "visits remain restricted to holidays and specially authorized dates"; "access was limited to organized tours held during the intermediate days of Sukkot"
notes: Secondary (news), not an IDF order. Har Dov = Shebaa Farms per Wikipedia: 'Israel refers to this northern, higher part as Har Dov (Mount Dov)'. Whether the lookout lies inside the register's outline was not checked. In Oct 2023 the IDF declared the area up to 4 km from the Lebanon border closed ('entry into the area is prohibited', Israel National News flash 616855, 15 Oct 2023, summary); whether that order still stands was not found. On the Lebanese side, an LBC report describes an Israeli-imposed 'red line' farmers and herders cannot cross (not opened). FCDO advice is only advice.

question: legal_basis_refuges
answer: National wildlife refuges: entry without authorisation is trespass under federal regulation; a permit is required unless the regulations open the refuge.
publisher: 50 CFR 26.21 (U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service), via Cornell LII
quote: No person shall trespass, including but not limited to entering, occupying, using, or being upon, any national wildlife refuge, except as specifically authorized in this subchapter C
notes: 50 CFR 26.22(b): 'A permit shall be required for any person entering a national wildlife refuge' unless subchapter C provides otherwise (summary quote). Applies to all nine UM refuges.

question: legal_basis_defense_areas
answer: Johnston Island, Kingman Reef, Midway Island and Wake Island are Naval Defensive Sea Areas and Naval Airspace Reservations (Executive Orders). Entry restrictions are suspended for Wake except foreign-flag ships and foreign nationals; not suspended for Johnston, Kingman, Midway.
publisher: 32 CFR 761.7 (Department of the Navy), via Cornell LII
quote: No person, except persons aboard public vessels or aircraft of the United States, shall enter any defense area.
notes: Exception: persons 'issued an authorization to enter by an Entry Control Commander' (summary). Areas from 32 CFR 761.3(a); suspensions from 761.4(d) (summary, https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/32/761.4). 761.4(c): 'Entry into Johnston Atoll is controlled by the Defense Nuclear Agency' (text is dated; the agency no longer exists). eCFR was blocked; LII copy read.

question: scheduled_transport
answer: no ordinary scheduled route found. publisher: Aerovías DAP, 'Programa Full Day Antártica' 2026-2027 (operator's own document)
quote: Los pasajeros que no estén presentes en esta reunión no podrán ser partícipes del tour contratado.

question: visitor_access_2025_2026
answer: unknown; no primary source (Croatian police, ministry or court) found on current access. Secondary sources conflict: Wikivoyage says Croatia opened land access on 6 Aug 2023 for anyone checking out of Croatia, with non-EU visitors detained; Wikipedia (citing The Times, 25 Jun 2024) says more than 200 people accessed it in March 2024; Croatian police demolished structures and made arrests on 21-22 Sep 2023.
quote: As of 6 August 2023 the border was opened by Croatia to anyone who legally checks out of Croatia
notes: Secondary only; Wikivoyage cites no source. Wikipedia Liberland (summary): 'Liberland movement supporters and journalists managed to obtain unofficial access to the land parcel' (Aug 2023) and 'More than 200 people successfully accessed the territory during Jedlička's attempt to land on Liberland in March' (2024); it has nothing on 2025-2026. The only Croatian primary found is MVEP's statement of June 2015 (https://mvep.gov.hr/nieuws/163069): the right bank 'is currently under the control of the Croatian border police'; visitors must 'abide by Croatian laws and EU regulations' on border crossing (summary); it neither permits nor bans entry. A search summary reports 2016 appeal rulings that crossing into Liberland from Croatia is illegal (not opened, unverified). Wikivoyage: water crossing from Serbia not allowed. Recommendation: keep the register value as is until a primary source is found; 'closed' is not confirmed by an act either.
